title: Underlying finite limits and small colimits of flat groupoid modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ a groupoid in schemes over $S$ [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Let $\mathcal C$ have objects $(M,\beta)$, where $M$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $\beta:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $e^*\beta=1$, and $c^*\beta=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\beta\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\beta$ under the canonical pullback identifications. Its morphisms $f:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ satisfy $s^*f\circ\beta=\gamma\circ t^*f$. Write $V:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ for the forgetful functor. Assume $s,t$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then $\mathcal C$ is abelian; $V$ is faithful, reflects isomorphisms, and computes kernels, cokernels, finite direct sums, and finite limits as those of the underlying $\mathcal O_U$-modules. It also computes every small colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] as the colimit of the underlying $\mathcal O_U$-modules, which is quasi-coherent. In particular, a pullback of equivariant modules is the underlying module pullback with its induced equivariant structure, and a cocone of equivariant modules whose underlying module cocone is a colimit is itself a colimit. All diagrams and their morphism sets are small in a fixed universe containing the schemes and modules.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), their constructions on underlying quasi-coherent modules; faithfulness and reflection of isomorphisms follow from the displayed definition of morphisms.

proof.text: Work in the chosen universe. The ambient category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$ is abelian and has small colimits. Kernels and cokernels of maps between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent, as are small direct sums. In particular every small diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ has a quasi-coherent ambient colimit: put $A=\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}D_i$, $B=\bigoplus_iD_i$, and define $d:A\to B$ on the summand for $a:i\to j$ by $\iota_jD(a)-\iota_i$. Then $L=\operatorname{coker}d$ is quasi-coherent by the cokernel theorem. A map $B\to N$ kills $d$ precisely when its components form a cocone, proving that $L$ is the ambient colimit. This also handles the empty diagram, giving zero.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: Every scheme pullback preserves quasi-coherence. It preserves small colimits because it is left adjoint to module pushforward; hence it preserves cokernels and finite sums. The tensor formula makes it additive. For a flat scheme map its stalk ring maps are flat, so the stated flat tensor-pullback theorem applies to this very functor and preserves kernels. These observations apply on $U$, on $R$, and on schemes of composable arrows. In particular, for $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ and $p_0,p_1:P\to R$, the projections are flat by base change of $t,s$. The composite $q=s p_1=s c$ is flat: at a point its stalk homomorphism is the composite of two flat ring maps, hence flat by the cited composition theorem. Thus $q^*$ preserves kernels.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: Equivariant maps are closed under sums, negatives, zero and composition by their defining equation and additivity of pullback. They therefore form an additive subgroup of each underlying module Hom group, with bilinear composition. Forgetting is faithful. If an equivariant map $f:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ has underlying inverse $g$, multiplying $s^*f\,\beta=\gamma\,t^*f$ by $s^*g$ on the left and $t^*g$ on the right gives $s^*g\,\gamma=\beta\,t^*g$. Thus $g$ is equivariant and $V$ reflects isomorphisms. Zero and a finite direct sum carry the zero and block-diagonal descent isomorphisms, using pullback preservation of finite sums from Step 2. Their unit and cocycle identities hold componentwise, and their inclusions and projections are equivariant. Their universal properties follow by taking components. The underlying finite sums are thus biproducts in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: Let $D_i=(M_i,\beta_i)$ be any small equivariant diagram and let $(L,\iota_i)$ be its ambient module colimit from Step 1. Pullback preservation gives colimits $(t^*L,t^*\iota_i)$ and $(s^*L,s^*\iota_i)$. Define $b:t^*L\to s^*L$ by $b\,t^*\iota_i=s^*\iota_i\,\beta_i$. These maps are compatible since every transition map is equivariant. The same construction with $\beta_i^{-1}$ yields an inverse, as the two composites are identity after every colimit leg. To prove $e^*b=1$, precompose with each $\iota_i$ and use $e^*\beta_i=1$. To prove $c^*b=p_1^*b\,p_0^*b$, precompose with each $(tc)^*\iota_i$ and use the corresponding identity for $\beta_i$ together with $t c=t p_0$, $s p_0=t p_1$, $s c=s p_1$. These legs jointly detect equality because all the composite pullbacks preserve colimits, by the same adjunction argument. Hence $(L,b)$ is an object and its legs are equivariant.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: For an equivariant cocone $h_i:(M_i,\beta_i)\to(N,\gamma)$, the ambient colimit gives a unique module map $h:L\to N$ with $h\iota_i=h_i$. The maps $s^*h\,b$ and $\gamma\,t^*h$ agree after each $t^*\iota_i$, by equivariance of $h_i$ and the defining equation for $b$. Since $t^*$ preserves this colimit, they are equal. Thus $h$ is equivariant; uniqueness is the underlying uniqueness. This proves the colimit universal property in $\mathcal C$. The identical argument applies to any already equivariant cocone whose underlying module cocone is a colimit: use its given structure in place of $b$. Consequently every such cocone is a colimit, as claimed.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: For $f:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ let $k:K\to M$ be the underlying module kernel, which is quasi-coherent. By Step 2, $t^*k$ and $s^*k$ are kernels of $t^*f$ and $s^*f$. The equation for $f$ shows that $\beta\,t^*k$ factors uniquely through $s^*k$; call the factor $\kappa:t^*K\to s^*K$. Applying the same construction with $\beta^{-1},\gamma^{-1}$ gives its inverse, since the composites become identity after the kernel inclusions. Thus $\kappa$ is an isomorphism and $s^*k\,\kappa=\beta\,t^*k$.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: The kernel structure obeys the laws. Pulling its defining equation back by $e$, and using $se=te=1_U$ and $e^*\beta=1$, gives $k\,e^*\kappa=k$; cancel the monomorphism $k$. On $P$ compare $c^*\kappa$ with $p_1^*\kappa\,p_0^*\kappa$. Postcomposition with $(sc)^*k$ makes both equal, by the defining equation for $\kappa$ and the cocycle of $\beta$. This postcomposition can be cancelled: $sc=q$ is flat by Step 2, and $q^*k$ is a kernel inclusion. Notice that no flatness of $e$ is asserted. Finally an equivariant $x:(T,\delta)\to(M,\beta)$ killed by $f$ has a unique underlying factor $y:T\to K$. Postcomposing $s^*y\,\delta$ and $\kappa\,t^*y$ with the monomorphism $s^*k$ gives equal maps by equivariance of $x$. Hence $y$ is equivariant and $(K,\kappa),k$ is a kernel in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: Apply Steps 4 and 5 to the parallel equivariant maps $f,0:M\rightrightarrows N$. Their underlying coequalizer is the module cokernel $p:N\to Q$, and $Q$ is quasi-coherent. Thus this construction equips the underlying cokernel with descent and makes $p$ a cokernel in $\mathcal C$. Explicitly its isomorphism $\lambda$ satisfies $\lambda\,t^*p=s^*p\,\gamma$. The unit and cocycle checks are those of Step 4; all pullbacks preserve the cokernel, so the necessary epimorphism cancellations are valid without extra flatness. We have now constructed all kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts on underlying modules.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: To check the abelian axioms, suppose $f$ is monic in $\mathcal C$. Its kernel inclusion $k$ is zero by cancellation of $f$, hence $1_K=0$ since $k$ is monic. The underlying kernel is therefore zero, so the underlying $f$ is monic in the ambient abelian category. There $M\to\ker(\operatorname{coker}f)$ is an isomorphism. The comparison is equivariant by the kernel universal property proved above, and Step 3 makes it an isomorphism in $\mathcal C$. Thus $f$ is a kernel of its cokernel. Dually, if $f$ is epic, its cokernel projection is zero, its cokernel object has identity zero, and the underlying $f$ is epic. The ambient isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}(\ker f)\to N$ is equivariant by the cokernel universal property and is an isomorphism by Step 3. Hence every epi is a cokernel. Together with the preadditivity, zero object, finite biproducts, kernels and cokernels already constructed, these are precisely the abelian axioms.

source.place: Tag 077R (lemma-colimits), Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), with their omitted universal-property and cocycle verifications written out.

proof.text: Finite limits also have the required underlying form. For a finite diagram $D:J\to\mathcal C$, form $B=\bigoplus_{j\in J}D_j$ and $E=\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}D_j$ and the equivariant map $d:B\to E$ whose $a$-component is $D(a)\pi_i-\pi_j$. The kernel $L\to B$ with its component projections is a limit: a map to $B$ factors through $L$ exactly when its components obey every cone equation, and its factor is unique. The same formula in ambient modules proves that $V$ computes this limit. Empty $J$ gives zero, the terminal object. For $M\xrightarrow{f}T\xleftarrow{g}N$, the formula is the familiar kernel of $[f,-g]:M\oplus N\to T$ with its two projections, so it gives the underlying module pullback with induced equivariance. This proves all finite-limit clauses.
